title: The Wolf of the Glass Steppe
premise: Xanthe Fairweather poisons herself daily by design: as royal food-taster, she sips toxins to build immunity, safe inside the valley where magic cannot follow. But when the old gods resume answering prayers, the palace's immunity to their power begins to fail, and Xanthe's carefully cultivated poisons start working in reverse—granting her visions of a country that was unmade a century ago. Hunted by a god who wants a living doorway, accompanied by a disgraced cartographer and a child who remembers the erased nation, she must cross the Glass Steppe to find the door out of Vhaloria before the moon completes its thirteenth turn. In the end she opens the door, but refuses to pass through it, instead unmaking herself as taster and remaking herself as the valley's new boundary-keeper—choosing a family made, not found.
about_author: Xanthe Delacroix is the pen name of a former line cook who spent a decade working palace-adjacent catering jobs and swears every kitchen is haunted by at least one dead empire. She writes fantasy about people whose survival depends on swallowing things they shouldn't.

chapters.title: A Measured Spoonful
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. We open in the palace kitchens as she tastes the king's supper—hemlock in the honeyed quail, her fourteenth poison—and catalogues her symptoms with clinical calm. Establish her invisibility as armor and the valley's magic-dead stillness. Emotional beat: the strange pride of a body that survives everything and belongs nowhere.

chapters.title: The Prayer That Answered Back
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. A scullery maid prays to the old gods at the kitchen hearth, and something answers—the first answered prayer in a hundred years. The candles gutter blue; the maid's burn heals. Xanthe, immune by training to everything except this, feels it like a hook behind her ribs. Emotional beat: dread dressed as curiosity.

chapters.title: What the King Cannot Taste
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. The king's food begins tasting of snow and iron—flavors from a country that no longer exists. Xanthe reports nothing, because reporting means attention, and attention is death for a taster. She starts secretly recording the flavors in a recipe book. Emotional beat: the first crack in her policy of invisibility.

chapters.title: The Cartographer of Nowhere
chapters.summary: Ilya Vosk's POV. Introduce the disgraced royal cartographer imprisoned for mapping Vhaloria, the erased nation, on official charts. He's been waiting eleven years for someone to ask him why the maps keep redrawing themselves. He notices Xanthe watching him in the archive. Emotional beat: bitter hope rediscovering its voice.

chapters.title: Thirteen Moons, Twelve Gone
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. An astronomer-priest announces the moon has begun a thirteenth turn—a turn that belongs to no calendar, a turn the old gods are owed. Xanthe's poisons begin showing her visions of Vhalorian kitchens, its people mid-meal. Emotional beat: the vertigo of learning your survival skill has become a haunting.

chapters.title: The Child Who Remembers
chapters.summary: Shared POV. Xanthe finds a kitchen orphan, Sef, who speaks fluent Vhalorian in his sleep—a language no living teacher exists for. He draws the door she's been seeing in her visions. The god's hook behind her ribs tightens. Emotional beat: two invisible people recognizing each other.

chapters.title: Poison as Prayer
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. The palace priest discovers her vision-taint and declares her a vessel; the king orders her confined for the god's use. Xanthe realizes staying was always the dangerous choice. She frees Ilya, takes Sef, and flees through the scullery gate at moonrise. Emotional beat: terror and exhilaration of the first irreversible act.

chapters.title: The Edge of the Valley
chapters.summary: Ilya's POV. The trio reaches the valley's boundary—the line where magic cannot follow. Crossing it means Xanthe's trained immunities may fail, since some were magic-adjacent all along. She steps over anyway. The world floods with sensation and old power. Emotional beat: the cost of safety made suddenly, physically real.

chapters.title: The Glass Steppe
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. The steppe: a plain of fused sand where Vhaloria was unmade, mirror-flat, reflecting not the travelers but the country as it was. They walk on the sky of a dead nation. Sef navigates by memories that aren't his. Emotional beat: grief for a home none of them had.

chapters.title: The God Who Hungers Politely
chapters.summary: Shared POV. The god—Vhal, last of the old gods—appears as a courteous host at an impossible dinner table, offering rest, food, belonging. He only wants Xanthe to open the door; the country needs a living key. Ilya refuses for her; the dinner ends. Emotional beat: temptation that feels like kindness.

chapters.title: What Immunity Costs
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Crossing the boundary, Xanthe's built immunities begin to unravel—her body purging decades of poison, leaving her feverish, weeping, human. Sef nurses her. She confesses she never chose to be a taster; she was sold to the palace at seven. Emotional beat: the armor coming off, and surviving it.

chapters.title: The Cartographer's Confession
chapters.summary: Ilya's POV. Ilya admits he didn't map Vhaloria from records—he mapped it from memory. He was born there, smuggled out as a child, and his charts were prayers. The god has been answering him for years. Emotional beat: shame transformed into shared purpose.

chapters.title: The Village That Isn't
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. They find a settlement on the steppe: people who refused to leave when Vhaloria was unmade, living inside the reflection. They offer the trio a meal—the first food Xanthe has ever eaten that no one wanted her to die for. Emotional beat: belonging offered, and distrusted.

chapters.title: The Turn of the Moon
chapters.summary: Shared POV. The thirteenth moon reaches fullness early; the god grows impatient and begins pulling Vhaloria's reflection over the real world, village and all. The steppe's glass begins to crack. The villagers beg Xanthe to open the door and end the waiting. Emotional beat: the weight of being needed by everyone.

chapters.title: Recipes for the Dead
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. In the village, Xanthe cooks Vhalorian dishes from her vision-flavors, and the food restores the villagers' true memories—the god has been feeding on their forgetting. Cooking becomes resistance. Sef remembers his grandmother's kitchen and weeps. Emotional beat: nourishment as an act of defiance.

chapters.title: The Door in the Reflection
chapters.summary: Ilya's POV. Ilya's final map reveals the door's location: it was never in Vhaloria. It is in the valley, in the palace kitchens, in the hearth where the maid prayed. They must go back through the god's gathering storm. Emotional beat: the terrible comedy of the answer being home.

chapters.title: Running Before the Thirteenth Moon
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. The race back across the cracking steppe, the god's reflection chasing them like weather. The villagers hold the glass bridge open at the cost of their refuge. Sef falters; Xanthe carries him. Emotional beat: found family tested at a dead run.

chapters.title: The Hearth Where It Began
chapters.summary: Shared POV. They slip into the palace as the thirteenth moon peaks; the kitchens are full of kneeling servants praying to Vhal. The door stands open in the hearth, and through it, Vhaloria waits—real, warm, lit. The god offers Xanthe everything she has never had: a home, a name, a table of her own. Emotional beat: the climax of temptation.

chapters.title: The Taster's Choice
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Xanthe realizes the door needs a key who has swallowed a country's worth of grief—and she has, dish by dish, poison by poison. She steps toward it. Then she tastes the truth in the offered feast: Vhaloria's return would consume the valley, her found family included. Emotional beat: the moment before the refusal.

chapters.title: What She Swallowed
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV, climax. Xanthe refuses—but instead of closing the door, she swallows the thirteenth moon's light as she once swallowed poison, taking Vhaloria's grief into her own body so the dead country can rest instead of return. Vhal, unburdened, fades into the hearth's ordinary fire. The door closes gently, like a book. Emotional beat: sacrifice that is also a homecoming.

chapters.title: Boundary-Keeper
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Aftermath: the valley's magic-dead stillness now lives in Xanthe herself, and she becomes its keeper, the living line the old powers cannot cross. The king pardons Ilya, who redraws Vhaloria's maps as memorial rather than summons. Sef is adopted—by all three of them, informally, permanently. Emotional beat: quiet joy after enormous cost.

chapters.title: A Table of Her Own
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. One year later: Xanthe cooks a meal in her own kitchen at the valley's edge—no one's taster, no one's vessel. Ilya brings new charts; Sef brings stolen pastries. The thirteenth moon rises, and it is only a moon. Emotional beat: the price of survival, paid in full, and worth it.
